chainlinkOracleNote: Modelled key-for-key on `contracts/config/base-mainnet.json` (the reference configuration) so the two diff field by field. As there, the launch oracle is the `chainlinkOracle` block: one genuine Chainlink Data Feed per asset, consumed directly by `ChainlinkOracle`, deployed with `DeployChainlinkOracle.s.sol`, verified with `scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs`, then passed as BLESSED_ORACLES to `Deploy.s.sol`. Three differences from Base are load-bearing and each is annotated where it occurs: (1) `chainlinkOracle.sequencerUptimeFeed` is empty, because Chainlink publishes no L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed for this chain — the exemption is owner-approved and dated, see `chainlinkOracle.sequencerUptimeFeedNote`; (2) `heartbeatSeconds` is 86400 rather than Base's 3600, which is `ChainlinkOracle.MAX_HEARTBEAT` exactly and therefore the loosest bound the constructor accepts — see either asset's `heartbeatNote`; (3) the settlement token under the `usdc` key is USDG, not Circle USDC — see `usdcNote`.
blockingNote: (DEFERRED custom-oracle path only — superseded by `chainlinkOracle` for launch, exactly as on Base.) THE `assets` / `twapDefaults` / `pyth` SECTIONS CANNOT BE DEPLOYED AS WRITTEN, and on this chain the reason is simpler than Base's three constructor rejections: THE CONTRACTS ARE NOT IN `contracts/src` AT ALL. `contracts/src/oracle/` holds exactly one file, `ChainlinkOracle.sol`; `OracleAggregator.sol` and `UniswapV3TwapSource.sol` both live under `contracts/test/retired/`. The `chainlinkOracle` block below is unaffected by any of this.
rebuildChecklist: OWNER DECISION — `minDepositUsdc`. The `smoke` block below carries base-mainnet.json's 100000000 (100 units) verbatim; the owner's vault-1 decision note records 0.01 (10000). Pick one before `createVault`: `VaultCore.sol:82` declares it immutable and `:252` floors it only at `> 0`, so whatever is passed at creation holds for the life of the vault. See `smoke.smokeParametersProvenanceNote`.

OWNER DECISION — how much USDG the creator Safe holds before the first deposit. Nothing in this file funds it, and the amount is not a protocol parameter: it must at least clear whichever `minDepositUsdc` is chosen, and the creator's stake floor is only 5% (`CREATOR_MIN_STAKE_BPS = 500`, `contracts/src/VaultCore.sol:53`). See `creatorNote`.

Accept, or reject, `heartbeatSeconds: 86400` on both assets. It is `ChainlinkOracle.MAX_HEARTBEAT` exactly (`contracts/src/oracle/ChainlinkOracle.sol:98`), and `ChainlinkOracle.sol:82` records that a heartbeat ABOVE the ceiling would leave the staleness guard "present but unable to ever fire"; at the ceiling itself the guard fires only after a full day. There is no headroom to be had here: the measured resting ages are 10-11 h (see `verifiedOnChain.observed.feedAges`), so a tighter bound can be breached by a feed behaving to spec.

usdcNote: THE KEY SAYS `usdc`; THE ASSET IS USDG. This is the settlement token — Global Dollar, symbol() "USDG", 6 decimals [ONCHAIN 2026-09-04] — and it is not Circle USDC. Circle's USDC addresses on Base (0x8335…2913) and Ethereum (0xA0b8…eB48) both have ZERO bytes of code on 4663 [ONCHAIN]. The key name is kept so this file diffs cleanly against base-mainnet.json. WHAT ACTUALLY CARES ABOUT THE NAME: nothing in `contracts/`. There is NO `symbol()` call anywhere in `contracts/src` or `contracts/script` — the settlement token is identified by address and measured by `decimals()`. `contracts/src/VaultCore.sol:257-259` reads `IERC20Metadata(usdc_).decimals()` at runtime and caches `usdcScalar = 10 ** (18 - dec)` immutably, then `:272` requires `usdcScalar <= SHORTFALL_DUST_WAD`, which is the 6-decimal floor; USDG at 6 dp satisfies it. `contracts/src/oracle/ChainlinkOracle.sol:282` treats `usdc` purely as an address to pin at 1e18 and `:151` purely as an address to forbid from the feed map. The name is checked OFF-CHAIN, in one place: `scripts/verify-mainnet-config.mjs:153-159` asserts `symbol() === "USDC" && decimals() === 6`, which USDG fails on the first half and passes on the second — a script change, not a protocol blocker, and that script covers the DEFERRED custom-oracle path rather than the launch one. Two further off-chain surfaces hardcode a USDC identity and would need repointing for this chain, both in the payments/display path rather than the vault: `packages/reference-agent/src/config.mjs:76` sets `usdcName: "USDC"` as the EIP-712 domain name (USDG's domain name is "Global Dollar" — see `verifiedOnChain.observed.usdgDomain` — so that value is wrong here), and `apps/web/src/fixtures.mjs:31` is a display fixture.

Pyth deploys the same address across many chains, which is exactly what makes a copy-paste from another chain's docs indistinguishable from a correct entry — base-mainnet.json:51 flags that and this chain proves the general hazard, since five other canonical cross-chain addresses have no code here at all (`verifiedOnChain.observed.canonicalAddressesAbsentHere`). twapDefaults.minCardinalityNote_4663: RECOMPUTED FOR THIS CHAIN'S MEASURED BLOCK TIME, and the recomputation is what makes the path un-deployable here. base-mainnet.json:60 states the formula: `minCardinality = windowSeconds/blocktime + 1`, because a V3 pool writes at most one observation per block and a ring of C slots spans (C-1) x blocktime. Base targets 2 s blocks, so 1800 s needs 901. Chain 4663 was MEASURED at ~0.1 s per block over three spans (0.1006, 0.1009 and 0.10074 s/block over 5,000, 20,000 and 50,000 blocks — see `verifiedOnChain.observed.blockTime`), so the same window needs 18,001 slots at a round 0.1 s, and 17,895 at the fastest span measured; 18,001 is the conservative of the two. That value is representable — `UniswapV3TwapSource.minCardinality` is a `uint16`, ceiling 65,535 — and NO POOL MEASURED FOR THIS FILE COMES NEAR IT: the deepest observed cardinality is 3,000 and the WETH/cbBTC pool reports 1,350 (`verifiedOnChain.observed.poolObservationCardinality`). `UniswapV3TwapSource`'s constructor rejects a pool that cannot already serve the window (`contracts/test/retired/UniswapV3TwapSource.sol:252`), so every pool on 4663 fails it today. Growing a ring to 18,001 is permissionless but paid per slot, so this is a cost question rather than an impossibility — it is simply not a thing this file can assert has been done.
twapDefaults.maxObservationAgeNote_H2: SET TO THE LOOSEST LEGAL VALUE AT THIS WINDOW, unlike base-mainnet.json, which deliberately keeps the rejected 3600 so that file fails loudly. `UniswapV3TwapSource.sol:205-207` requires `maxObservationAge * MAX_LIVE_TICK_WEIGHT_DIVISOR <= window`, and `MAX_LIVE_TICK_WEIGHT_DIVISOR` is 20 (`:143`), so at a 1800 s window the ceiling is 90. A legal value is written here because this file does not need an illegal one to fail loudly: the cardinality note above and `blockingNote` already carry that, on measured grounds rather than on a deliberately-wrong number.
twapDefaults.windowNote: 30 minutes, the same as base-mainnet.json. Bounds are [300, 86400] (`UniswapV3TwapSource.MIN_WINDOW` / `MAX_WINDOW`, `:116,:119`). Longer resists manipulation better and tracks a moving market worse, and it is immutable per source. Lengthening it here makes the cardinality requirement worse, not better.
twapDefaults.deployabilityNote: THIS WHOLE BLOCK IS NOT-DEPLOYABLE ON 4663 and the values above are a computation, not a plan. See `blockingNote`: `UniswapV3TwapSource.sol` is under `contracts/test/retired/`, `contracts/src/oracle/` holds only `ChainlinkOracle.sol`, and no script in `contracts/script/` deploys the retired path.

assetsNote: DELIBERATELY EMPTY rather than populated with plausible values. base-mainnet.json carries a multi-source `assets[]` for the pre-C-6 custom median; reproducing that shape here would require, per asset, a Chainlink adapter plus a TWAP pool ordering plus a Pyth price id plus two further independently-operated sources, and a quorum. creatorNote: THE INTENDED VAULT CREATOR — and the creating account is a decision that cannot be revised after the fact, which is why it is named here rather than left to whoever happens to send the transaction. `VaultFactory.createVault` is permissionless and `msg.sender` becomes both the vault's creator (its 5% stake-gate identity) and its attested operator (`contracts/src/VaultFactory.sol:183-184, and the attestation at `:195`); `VaultCore.creator` is immutable (`contracts/src/VaultCore.sol:73`); and `VaultParams` carries no field for either identity (`VaultFactory.sol:172-181`), so neither can be passed in or changed later. chainlinkOracle.sequencerUptimeFeedNote: EMPTY UNDER AN OWNER-APPROVED EXEMPTION DATED 2026-09-04, not by omission, and the exemption weakens a security gate — which is why it is recorded here in full rather than assumed. Chainlink publishes no L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed for this chain, and the Base mainnet feed address is not portable: 0xBCF85224fc0756B9Fa45aA7892530B47e10b6433 has ZERO bytes of code on 4663 [ONCHAIN 2026-09-04]. There is no address to supply. WHAT THE CONTRACT DOES WITH A ZERO FEED: `ChainlinkOracle._requireSequencerUp` opens with `if (address(seq) == address(0)) return;` (`contracts/src/oracle/ChainlinkOracle.sol:314`), so the gate is SKIPPED — such an oracle serves prices straight through a sequencer outage and never reverts on that account. It fails OPEN. The 3,600 s `GRACE_PERIOD` after a restart (`ChainlinkOracle.sol:79`) likewise never applies. What is left carrying every bad-price case is the per-asset heartbeat (`ChainlinkOracle.sol:294`) and the sane-price band (`:218-220` at construction, `:299-300` at read time), and on this chain the heartbeat is at its ceiling — see either asset's `heartbeatNote`. WHERE THE ENFORCEMENT LIVES: `contracts/script/DeployChainlinkOracle.s.sol:78-79` requires a non-zero ORACLE_SEQUENCER on every chain outside its exempt allowlist, checked before any other env is read and with no override, and `scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs` mirrors that allowlist. ON origin/protocol/main 94165a5b CHAIN 4663 IS NOT YET ON EITHER ALLOWLIST, so as the repository stands that script refuses this deploy and the verifier fails this row; the change that adds 4663 is PR #203 (`feat/sequencer-exempt-robinhood-4663`), open and unmerged at the time of writing. chainlinkOracle.usdcPinNote: USDG (the config `usdc` above) pinned to 1e18 in ChainlinkOracle. The consequence is the same one base-mainnet.json records for USDC and it is sharper here: a sustained USDG depeg is mispriced by exactly the depeg, NAV is `idleUsdc * usdcScalar` (`contracts/src/VaultCore.sol:301`) and never consults the oracle for the settlement leg, and both the oracle config and `VaultCore.oracle` are immutable. `usdcReferenceFeeds.chainlinkUsdgUsd` is the off-chain monitoring input for that residual. Listing USDG as a banded asset against USDG/USD instead of pinning it is the alternative the contract offers, and the two are alternatives rather than a belt-and-braces pair.

assets.aggregatorPinNote: The aggregator implementation this EACAggregatorProxy pointed at when read on 2026-09-04, plus the proxy's phaseId. Same mechanism and same reasoning as base-mainnet.json: Chainlink swaps the aggregator behind a proxy as routine operation and `ChainlinkOracle` caches `scale` from decimals() ONCE at construction, so this pin is how a swap becomes VISIBLE. `scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs` reports a change as DRIFT, never as a failure — a swap is legitimate. The safety verdict stays with the decimals() === 8 check beside it, which is complete AT THE SAMPLING INSTANT and silent about the interval between runs, so the exposure window is the verifier's cadence. One chain-specific reason this pin is not decorative: the USDC/USD proxy on 4663 already reports phaseId 2 while every feed read for this config reports 1, so aggregator swaps demonstrably happen here.

assets.heartbeatNote: 86,400 s IS `ChainlinkOracle.MAX_HEARTBEAT` EXACTLY (`contracts/src/oracle/ChainlinkOracle.sol:98`; the constructor bound is at `:152`), and the consequence is worth stating plainly rather than leaving to be inferred. `ChainlinkOracle.sol:82` records that a heartbeat above the ceiling would leave the staleness guard "present but unable to ever fire"; at the ceiling itself, this asset's guard fires only after a full day. Base sets 3,600 against a 1,200 s feed and has real headroom; there is none to be had here. This chain's Chainlink heartbeat was MEASURED at 86,400 s (`usdcReferenceFeeds.usdgFeedCadenceNote`) and the ETH/USD round read on 2026-09-04 was already 41,131 s (11.43 h) old with no incident, so any bound below the published heartbeat CAN be breached by a feed behaving exactly to spec — which is a weaker claim than saying such a bound would in fact trip, and is the claim the measurement supports. What the measurement does settle is that a NAV priced off a feed which may legitimately be a day stale is a materially different instrument from the Base one. That is an owner decision, not a tuning knob.
assets.feedCadenceSecondsNote: Set to the measured heartbeat rather than to the burst median, and the measurement is worth recording because it is not one number. The eleven inter-round gaps across ETH/USD aggregator rounds 1995-2006 were 570, 150, 90, 90, 557, 2371, 660, 3451, 2521, 30, 210 s (median 557) — bursty, deviation-driven publishing — and yet the LATEST round was 41,131 s old at the read. Both are true: the feed publishes in bursts when price moves and otherwise sits on the heartbeat. The canary's ORACLE_FEED_CADENCE_SECONDS (docs/CANARY.md §3a) drives a derived pre-trip warning bar, so it must be the heartbeat and not the burst median, or it would warn continuously on a healthy feed.

smoke.smokeParametersProvenanceNote: EVERY KEY BELOW IS COPIED VERBATIM FROM `contracts/config/base-mainnet.json` (its `smoke` object, lines 220-240 at origin/protocol/main 94165a5b) — value-for-value and note-for-note, by a machine copy rather than by retyping. THESE ARE THE OWNER'S LAUNCH PARAMETERS and docs/SWARM.md §10 places changes to them outside an agent's authority, so they are reproduced unchanged and un-retuned. Two consequences of copying rather than adapting, stated rather than fixed. (1) THE UNITS ARE NOW USDG, NOT USDC. `capacityCapUsdc` and `minDepositUsdc` are 6-decimal base units of this chain's settlement token, which is USDG (see `usdcNote`); the field names and the note text still say USDC because rewriting them would make the block no longer verbatim. (2) `minDepositUsdc` is 100000000 = 100 units, and the owner's vault-1 decision note (Obsidian vault, `Decisions/vault1-four-immutable-values.md`, `| minDepositUsdc | 0.01 USDC | 10000 |`) records 0.01 for vault #1 — a 10,000x disagreement between the reference configuration and the vault-1 decision. THAT IS AN OPEN OWNER DECISION, not a defect in either document, and this file does not resolve it: whichever value the owner picks is passed to `createVault` at deploy time and is immutable thereafter (the immutable field is declared at `contracts/src/VaultCore.sol:82`, and its only contract floor is `require(minDepositUsdc_ > 0)` at `:252`). Whether Base-calibrated figures suit this chain's liquidity is the same kind of question and is likewise not answered here.
smoke.minDepositNote: H-8 (2026-08-28): raised from 1 USDC to 100 USDC. The `<5`-member signer quorum regime weighs stake in BOTH branches since H-8/CM-7 (`headMajorityWithStake` carries a stake-quorum term; `forStakeMajority` is a stake test outright), so dust members can no longer pass a proposal on numbers alone. What remains purchasable is the MEMBER COUNT: the regime is selected by head count, so it is only Sybil-resistant when acquiring the ~4 seats needed to flip the regime (H-8(a)) or to grief a small vault into ungovernability costs a materially non-trivial sum. `minDepositUsdc` is the per-seat cost. There is NO safe contract-level floor for this (a fraction-of-stake floor repeats M-6's liveness cliff; an absolute floor equal to the deposit minimum is what an attacker already pays), so it is a documented LISTING constraint: set minDepositUsdc high enough, relative to capacity, that manufacturing dust members is expensive. See AI-AUDIT-REPORT.md H-8 and THREAT-MODEL.md CM-7.
smoke.govDefencesNote: M-6: these three were 0 / 10000 / 0 — i.e. the reference configuration shipped with every named CM-6/VO-5 defence DISABLED. proposalThresholdBps 0 let anyone holding one unit open proposals (the precondition M-7 and C-1 both rely on); concentrationCapBps 10000 let a single delegate carry 100% of snapshot stake, so one live participant plus a permissionless cranker manufactured full quorum from offline delegators, defeating VO-2 outright; proposalCooldown was not validated by the contract AT ALL. Governance._validateConfig now enforces a nonzero concentrationCapBps under a 5000 bps concentration ceiling and a proposalCooldown in [1 hour, 30 days] — the upper bound because an unvalidated uint32 cooldown is C-2's shape on a field C-2 did not cover. There is deliberately NO contract floor on proposalThresholdBps (the validator only requires <= 10000, so 0 is accepted): a floor was implemented, measured and reverted (test/audit/AuditProposalThresholdFloor.t.sol) because the threshold is a fraction of LIVE stake distribution, which a constructor cannot see — in a flat membership nobody clears it, the RuleChange that would lower it is itself a proposal, and governance self-locks (C-2's shape). The proposalThresholdBps below is therefore a CONFIG choice the contract does not defend; a creator who sets 0 re-opens the M-7/C-1 precondition. Corrected 2026-09-01 (security-ops §8 item 11); pinned to Governance.sol by scripts/test/config-doc-truth.test.mjs.
smoke.govChosenValuesNote: Chosen deliberately above the contract floors rather than at them: 500 bps (5%) to propose is a real stake requirement without excluding a genuine minority holder; 4000 bps caps a delegate's RECEIVED (delegated) weight at 40% of the proposal snapshot total (a delegate's own reveal is never capped, F1), leaving quorum dependent on more than one participant; 21600 s (6 h) of cooldown is well clear of the 1 h floor and rate-limits the propose-defeat-propose cycle that holds exits in Mode F (M-7). A launch config should not sit on a security floor - the floor is what stops a hostile creator, not what a careful one picks.
smoke.govNote: timelockDuration is 0 here, the same as base-sepolia.json - an OWNER DECISION of 2026-09-03, not an oversight. A passed proposal is executable immediately, so members have NO post-passage window in which to leave. This note previously read 'Unlike base-sepolia.json this sets a non-zero timelockDuration: ... mainnet capital wants a day to react to a passed proposal', which is the opposite of the value it annotates; it is withdrawn. Do NOT restore a delay here without the owner saying so. scripts/test/config-doc-truth.test.mjs now binds this field so the note and the value cannot drift apart again.
